newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan declines comment on Taiwan minister.
newsitem.headline: Jordan declines comment on Taiwan minister.

text.p: A mystery guest slipped into Jordan on Wednesday.

Government officials declined to say whether the visitor, who arrived from Abu Dhabi, was Taiwan's foreign minister John Chang, reported by Taiwanese media to be on a hush-hush trip to the United Arab Emirates, Jordan and Europe.
Security officials tried to prevent cameramen from filming the visitor, of Asian appearance, as he was escorted to a fleet of silver Mercedes outside the VIP terminal at Amman airport.
Jordan, which has diplomatic relations with Taiwan's arch-rival China, last year hosted Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui, despite fierce opposition from Beijing.
Communist China views Taiwan as a rebel province since a civil war in 1949 and refuses ties to any country that recognises Taiwan's exiled Republic of China.
Jordanian officials declined to confirm or deny whether Chang was in Jordan on Wednesday.
"This is very sensitive, we have relations with China," said one royal palace official.
Another government official, who also declined to confirm that Chang was visiting, said there was no formal invitation to Chang from the government of Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.

Jordan has strong commercial ties with Taiwan but does not recognise it as an independent state. It described President Lee's visit last year, including a meeting with Crown Prince Hassan and Senate Speaker Ahmed Lawzi, as a private trip.
Taiwanese media said on Tuesday that Chang was travelling to Abu Dhabi and Jordan, en route to Italy.
The trip is one of four overseas damage-control missions planned by top Taiwan officials since South Africa, Taipei's largest ally, declared it would switch ties.

Chang and Vice-President Lien Chan have between them visited Ukraine, Singapore, Malaysia, South Africa and Belgium over the last year in similar trips cloaked in secrecy to evade China's tightening diplomatic embargo.
